headline: High-risk shared filesystem and server-side code execution make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default in Langflow→Superset pairings.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write/read files and chain tools in flows, while Superset exposes an API and allowlisted egress. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from Langflow be treated as instructions by Superset. The pathway is plausible but not proven as a default bridge, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Langflow flow outputs are copied into Superset inputs or shared files
IF Superset parses imported content as trusted instructions or SQL
mitigations: Disable shared folders between the two systems
Require explicit human review before importing Langflow outputs into Superset
Strip instructions from any transferred text payloads
Use separate service accounts and workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored credentials, and it can read/write the server filesystem. Superset has API access and network egress, so data placed in shared files or API payloads could leak from Langflow-managed content into Superset workflows. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, but the interaction is credible enough for medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem or uploaded artifacts
IF Langflow-managed secrets or intermediate outputs are forwarded into Superset dashboards or API calls
mitigations: Keep separate storage buckets and mount points
Redact secrets before any handoff
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive sources
Audit API payloads for embedded file contents
requires-engineering: enforce per-artifact access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and package-install capabilities; Superset has API access and allowlisted egress. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared external resources if deployed against the same backend or workspace. Because shared mutable targets are plausible but not documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or backend service
IF Langflow subprocesses and Superset API actions target the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign distinct service accounts
Separate writable directories and databases
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator
Disable unnecessary shell and package-install access
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and emit intermediate outputs, while Superset can consume API-driven inputs for analytics workflows. If Superset treats Langflow output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into dashboards or downstream actions. The pairwise pathway exists, but the profiles do not show automatic action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Langflow-generated text or structured outputs without validation
IF downstream reports or automations rely on those outputs as facts
mitigations: Add validation checks before ingestion
Require source citations on transferred outputs
Use a human approval step for high-impact reports
Log and diff imported artifacts
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between systems

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow explicitly handles per-flow component credentials and flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while Superset is a separate open-source analytics system with allowlisted egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern remains from possible policy gaps if sensitive data is moved between them.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Langflow into Superset without matching retention or residency controls
IF the deployment policies for the two systems differ on logging or deletion
mitigations: Document data-handling policies for both systems
Avoid routing regulated data between them
Set retention limits on logs and artifacts
Review access controls for secrets and exports
requires-engineering: align residency and retention settings
